text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 decode latency > 10s for inference-west-2 (streaming stalls observed). Sev: high. Paging oncall.

tara: seeing this on dashboards too — p95 up from ~300ms -> 1.2s, p99 hitting 12-18s across multiple fleets. Streaming sessions are getting truncated or long gaps between chunks. :eyes:

hossein: noticed a bump correlated with last night's kernel rollout (kernel:v4.2.1 -> v4.3.0, includes new TRT 8.6 build and flashattn2 kernel). Canary had 5% traffic. Paging logs show increased compilepath misses and slower decode kernels.

dan: app logs show streaming stall loopbacks, clients get partial chunk then pause ~8-12s, then resume. No OOMs in node logs but dev runtime reports heavy compile cache churn.

liz: rolling back the kernel flag on canary now. Command: `kubectl set image ds/infer-runtime infer-runtime=runtime:v4.2.1-canary-rollback -n inference` — initiating.

kevin: putting routing rule to divert new requests to dedicated old kernel pool (region fallback). Patch:
```
PATCH /routing/traffic
{"match":"model:decode-*","route":"old-kernel-pool","percent":100}
```

sre-pager: FYI customers x-company and y-startup reported degraded streaming (support tickets 8623, 8624). We should assess impact and notify CS.

tara: quick notes from perf traces: decode kernel compile time up ~3-4x on first token, KV cache hit doesn't help because kernel recompile is happening due to new PTX variants. NVCC reported fallback to slower path for some attention kernels (FlashAttn2) — likely due to mismatched compute capability support.

hossein: suspected chain: TRT upgrade + new FlashAttn kernels + gcc/clang toolchain change -> different PTX -> longer JIT compile at first run -> memory pressure from compile cache eviction -> tail stalls. Also saw increased syscall latency on /dev/shm when temp kernel objects written.

dan: mitigation summary so far:
- rollback canary kernel image (liz) : in progress
- traffic diversion to old-kernel-pool (kevin) : applied
- disable FlashAttn2 fallback via runtime flag: `--enable-flashattn=false` on rollout (pending)
- increase compile cache size on nodes: `SYSCTL compile_cache_kb=8192` (investigating persistence)

liz: rollback completed on canary (5% -> 0%). Monitoring p99 now.

incident-bot: UPDATE: rollback job finished (job/rollback-1932468910), health checks passing.

kevin: p95 back to ~350ms after diversion; p99 improved to ~1.6s in the last 2m. Streaming stalls reduced but not eliminated — a handful of sessions still show 4-6s gaps.

hossein: still seeing compile churn on older nodes that serviced canary earlier; those nodes need cache warmup or restart. Suggest rolling restart to clear partial PTX artifacts: `kubectl rollout restart ds/infer-runtime -n inference --grace-period=30` on affected ASGs.

tara: can we identify which model variants are hitting worst? From traces: decode-large-v2 and chat-rt-13b-l2 on 2048 context had highest tail. Smaller models OK.

dan: looks like long sequences + attention kernel variations exacerbate JIT time. We should push an immediate narrow mitigation: reduce max_stream_chunk_size for streaming calls for affected models to avoid long single-chunk decode and give more opportunities for KV caching.

liz: changed per-model config to max_stream_chunk_size=256 for decode-large-v2/chat-rt-13b-l2. Deploying now.

sre-pager: CS update draft: "We observed a tail latency regression affecting streaming responses for some long-context workloads after a kernel/runtime kernel rollout. We've rolled back the canary and diverted traffic; most customers see improved latency. Support team will follow up with affected accounts." Want me to send? :+1:

tara: yes please, ask CS to include guidance: we recommend re-running warmup requests after the fix, and advise batching small streaming chunks until next stable runtime release.

kevin: telemetry note — capture pre/post flamegraphs and the compile cache hit rates for the next 2 hours and attach to the incident. I triggered a trace capture: `tracectl capture --inc 1932468910 --duration 120m`

hossein: next root-cause actions (proposed):
- block immediate rollout of runtime v4.3.0 until we validate toolchain (nvcc/ptx) combos across GPU fleet and TRT 8.6 flags.
- run controlled bench with FlashAttn2 disabled vs enabled across model shapes (512/1024/2048) and measure first-token compile time and steady-state.
- add runtime guard to avoid full JIT compile on first request: prefer loading precompiled kernel bundle if installed.
- increase compile cache size and persist across node restarts.

dan: agree. Also add automated test in CI that runs a quick decode trace for long sequences to catch compilepath regressions before rollout.

liz: handoff: I'm off in 35m. Next oncall please watch p99 for streaming sessions and coordinate with infra for node restarts. Tagging kevin to continue if anything flares.

kevin: will take handoff. I'll document follow-ups in the incident board and link traces + perf diffs.

sre-pager: INCIDENT NOTES (to record):
- Root cause (probable): TRT/FlashAttn kernel combo + new PTX/toolchain introduced in runtime v4.3.0 causing increased JIT/compile churn -> tail latency
- Customer impact: several customers experienced streaming stalls and p99 spikes to 10-18s; majority recovered after rollback and traffic diversion. Two support tickets opened.
- Mitigations applied: rollback canary, traffic diversion, per-model chunk-size reduction, slated node restarts and compile-cache bump.
- Next steps: bench matrix, toolchain compatibility sweep, CI regression test, runtime guard implementation, customer follow-up.

tara: adding notes to postmortem template. I'll start a /postmortem draft and assign owners.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: status=investigating -> mitigated. Assigned: kevin (owner), hossein (root-cause), dan (telemetry), liz (release follow-up). Handoff time: 1932472510

kevin: taking it. if anything spikes, @oncall escalate to infra and we'll do canary image hold. Logging final p99: 1.4s (stable) — continuing monitoring for 2h.
